structured_output.summary: Phase 15 delivers a genuinely accurate, security-conscious plan over a correctly pinned upstream delta, and its checks were really executed rather than asserted. I independently corroborated the delta claims: parent.yaml 40,867 lines vs openapi.yaml 41,567 (exactly the +700/-0 claimed), component-key counts 579 -> 589 (exactly 9 schemas + 1 parameter), no access-policy routes/schemas/tag in the parent, and the Portkey-Key securityScheme byte-identical in both files. Every substantive plan statement I sampled against contract.json held (12 query parameters, minimum:0 paging, 36/36/100/64/255 maximums, name 1..64, description nullable <=256, version minimum:1, MCP tools required vs provider models optional, ALL-or-nonempty-list oneOf, create-effect inference prose, fully optional response properties, no response-side defaults). The auth premise is real: the existing runtime key mechanism sends x-portkey-api-key (crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_runtime_contracts.rs:175). docs/checks/phase-15.json records six commands that exactly equal commands_for(15), all exit 0, which is what review_phase.check_evidence enforces; no SDK implementation leaked in, and fingerprint() covers untracked files so the new artifacts are bound to the reviewed SHA. The shortfalls are all in the phase's own named deliverables rather than in correctness: the pin records only self-referential SHA256 values and drops the gitBlobSha1 / sourceUrl / retrievedAt / license / bytes provenance the sibling vendor pin already establishes, so upstream identity cannot be verified even in principle from the recorded artifact; the "normalized contract with all references resolved" omits the Portkey-Key security scheme that every one of its five operations names; and the first-parent delta verifier fully diffs only paths and components.schemas plus three named parameters, leaving securitySchemes, the other parameters, tags and x-code-samples unchecked and asserting nothing about zero deletions. The rationale document is unreferenced by the plan, PHASES.md and scope_evidence, and git diff --check is vacuous for the untracked artifacts that are this phase's entire output. None of these is a blocker or high finding, but three mediums land directly on "pin sources/license", "verify the exact first-parent delta" and "all references resolved", so I cannot honestly score this at the threshold.

findings.description: The pin records only SHA256 values of the locally vendored bytes, which tools/portkey-access.mjs:12-14 then recomputes against the same local files. That detects later local tampering but is entirely self-referential: nothing in the artifact binds these bytes to upstream commit a27feb9. The repository's own established vendor convention does strictly more: contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/source.json:4-24 records repository, commit, upstreamPath, sourceUrl, sha256, gitBlobSha1, bytes, license, retrievedAt, yamlParser version, licensePath/licenseSha256, redistributed and usedForGeneration. gitBlobSha1 is the field that actually makes the pin verifiable offline against the upstream git object. The new pin has none of them, and no retrieval event is recorded at all. Phase 15's first named deliverable is "Pin sources/license", so this gap is in the core artifact. Separately, the retained LICENSE is 'The MIT License / Copyright (c) OpenAI (https://openai.com)' (contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/LICENSE:1-3) while source.json names Portkey-AI/openapi as the repository, and nothing records that provenance mismatch for the phase-17 NOTICE deliverable.
findings.required_fix: Extend source.json to the existing vendor convention: add schemaVersion, per-file sourceUrl, gitBlobSha1, bytes, retrievedAt, license ("MIT"), licensePath/licenseSha256, yamlParser {package, version}, redistributed and usedForGeneration, and a note that the retained LICENSE carries an OpenAI copyright inherited by Portkey-AI/openapi. Have tools/portkey-access.mjs recompute and assert gitBlobSha1 and bytes for each pinned file in addition to the SHA256 values.

findings.description: The first-parent delta verification is partial, so "verify the exact first-parent delta" is only partly machine-backed. Line 20 diffs every parent path and line 22 diffs every parent schema (both complete and strong), but line 25 compares only WorkspaceIdQuery, PageSize and CurrentPage out of all components.parameters, and nothing compares components.securitySchemes, info, servers, tags, the root security block, or x-code-samples. Nothing asserts AccessPolicyId is absent from the parent (parameters.slice(1) deliberately skips it, so a changed pre-existing AccessPolicyId would pass), nothing asserts exactly one parameter was added, and nothing asserts zero deletions. The commit does in fact also touch unverified regions: the tags list (contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/openapi.yaml:139) and the x-code-samples navigation groups (openapi.yaml:41307). I manually confirmed the unchecked regions are clean (securitySchemes identical at parent.yaml:22995 and openapi.yaml:23399; component-key counts 579 vs 589 = exactly 9 schemas + 1 parameter; line counts 40,867 vs 41,567 = exactly the claimed +700/-0), but a re-pin or a repeat run would not catch a regression there.
findings.required_fix: Make the verifier prove the whole-document delta: deep-compare parent to spec after removing the five routes, nine schemas, the AccessPolicyId parameter, the added tags entry and the added x-code-samples group, and fail on any other difference. Explicitly assert AccessPolicyId is absent from parent.components.parameters, that exactly one parameter was added, and that the spec line count equals the parent line count plus the recorded addition count with no deleted lines.

findings.description: The extracted contract is described in the plan (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:56-57) and in the phase-15 criteria (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:96-98) as "a normalized contract with all references resolved for this family", but components carries only schemas and parameters. Every one of the five operations declares security: [{"Portkey-Key": []}] (lines 23-27, 177-181, 358-362, 415-419, 502-506) and the scheme definition that gives that name meaning (apiKey, in: header, name: x-portkey-api-key, openapi.yaml:23399-23402) is not in the artifact. The authentication contract the phase-16 client is required to implement therefore exists only in plan and research prose, not in the machine-checked extraction, and tools/portkey-access.mjs:28 asserts the security names match but never the header they resolve to. No $ref dangles; this is specifically the security scheme.
findings.required_fix: Include components.securitySchemes.Portkey-Key in the extracted contract in tools/portkey-access.mjs:26, assert it is unchanged from the parent, and add a test_portkey_access.py assertion that the extracted scheme is apiKey/header/x-portkey-api-key so the phase-16 auth requirement is source-bound.

findings.description: Phase 15's scope_evidence lists only source.json, contract.json, the plan and the verifier. It omits the pinned sources themselves (openapi.yaml, parent.yaml, LICENSE), the gate test tools/test_portkey_access.py, and docs/portkey-access-policies-research.md. The research document is the phase's "record rationale" deliverable, yet a repository-wide grep finds no reference to it from the plan, docs/PHASES.md, docs/implementation-plan.md or phase-status.json, so it is unbound bookkeeping that a reviewer or successor phase has no path to. The same omission is repeated verbatim for phases 16 and 17 (lines 3209-3214, 3222-3227).
findings.required_fix: Add contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/{openapi.yaml,parent.yaml,LICENSE}, tools/test_portkey_access.py and docs/portkey-access-policies-research.md to the phase-15 scope_evidence, and link the research document from docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md so the recorded rationale is reachable from the plan.

findings.description: The phase-15 gate's whitespace checks are git diff --check and git diff --cached --check, but every artifact this phase produces is untracked (contracts/vendor/portkey-access/, tools/portkey-access.mjs, tools/test_portkey_access.py, docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md, docs/portkey-access-policies-research.md, docs/checks/phase-15.json). git diff does not see untracked files, so both recorded checks (docs/checks/phase-15.json:9-43, 0.006s and 0.003s) passed without examining any of the phase's output. I grepped the new files for trailing whitespace and found none, so this is a vacuous check rather than a missed defect.
findings.required_fix: Either stage the phase artifacts before running the gate so git diff --cached --check covers them, or add an explicit whitespace/newline assertion over the new plan, research, tooling and vendor files in tools/test_portkey_access.py.

findings.description: The gate suite is three thin tests. test_exact_operation_and_parameter_inventory asserts five operationIds, len(schemas)==9 and len(parameters)==12 but never the parameter names, verbs, routes, required/optional split or documented maximums that the plan enumerates (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:28-33), so a renamed or substituted query parameter would still pass. test_plan_contains_release_and_security_requirements (line 20) is a literal substring scan over the plan text, which pins prose rather than behavior and will pass on any reworded plan that happens to retain the tokens.
findings.required_fix: Assert the exact twelve query parameter names and their documented maxLength/minimum constraints, the verb-to-route-to-operationId mapping, the required property sets of CreateAccessPolicyRequest and UpdateAccessPolicyRequest, and the per-operation security name, all read from contract.json.

evidence: contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/parent.yaml is 40,867 lines and openapi.yaml is 41,567 lines (ripgrep line counts): a difference of exactly 700, matching the "adds 700 lines without deletions" claim in docs/portkey-access-policies-research.md:4.
Component-key counts at four-space indentation: parent.yaml 579, openapi.yaml 589 — exactly the claimed 9 new schemas plus 1 new parameter (docs/portkey-access-policies-plan.md:14-15).

parent.yaml contains no match for 'Access Policies', 'AccessPolicyId' or '/policies/access'; openapi.yaml matches at lines 139, 20007, 20135-20136, 20244, 20248, 20287, 20367, 23689 and 41308. AccessPolicyId exists only in openapi.yaml:23688, while PageSize/CurrentPage/WorkspaceIdQuery exist in both (parent 23101/23108/23284, spec 23505/23512/23696), so the slice(1) comparison in tools/portkey-access.mjs:25 is meaningful rather than vacuous.

components.securitySchemes.Portkey-Key is byte-identical in parent.yaml:22995-22998 and openapi.yaml:23399-23402 (apiKey, in: header, name: x-portkey-api-key), and the root security block is openapi.yaml:41028-41029 — none of which tools/portkey-access.mjs compares.

contract.json independently confirms the plan's typed-contract claims: twelve list query parameters (lines 182-284), page_size/current_page minimum 0 (lines 976-993), maxLength 36/36/100/64/255 (lines 215, 225, 235, 245, 255), name minLength 1 maxLength 64 (lines 717-718), description nullable maxLength 256 (lines 721-725), version minimum 1 (lines 762-765), MCP target requires type/server_id/tools (lines 628-632) while provider requires only type/provider_id (lines 667-670), ALL-or-nonempty-list oneOf (lines 646-661, 684-699), create effect inference prose (line 21), and no required list on AccessPolicy or AccessPolicyListItem (lines 804-954).

The only 'default' keyword in the entire extracted family is CreateAccessPolicyRequest.enabled: true (contract.json:748-751), confirming docs/portkey-access-policies-research.md:24-26 and the plan's claim at line 86-87 that both response default modes produce identical data.

docs/checks/phase-15.json records six commands whose 'command' arrays equal tools/check_phase.py:71-76 commands_for(15) element for element, all exit_code 0, with real captured stdout/stderr (the portkey verifier printed the five operations with Portkey-Key security and schemas:9; 30 review-gate tests and 3 portkey tests ran). tools/review_phase.py:99-113 enforces exactly that equality plus source_sha256 and source_unchanged, so the recorded set is complete for the registered gate.

tools/review_phase.py:43-60 hashes 'git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard', so the untracked vendor and tooling artifacts are inside the reviewed source fingerprint de5a8957…, excluding only docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json (lines 13-14).

tools/test_portkey_access.py:23-29 enforces no SDK implementation by diffing Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, crates/scm-sdk, LICENSE and NOTICE against baseline b65f3c98 and requiring no untracked files under those paths; git status shows no crates/ changes, so the 'No SDK implementation' criterion holds.

The plan's authentication premise is real, not assumed: the existing runtime key mechanism sends x-portkey-api-key (crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_runtime_contracts.rs:156, 175; crates/scm-sdk/tests/representative_clients.rs:407-412).

contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/source.json:4-24 establishes the repository's own vendor-pin convention (sourceUrl, gitBlobSha1, bytes, license, retrievedAt, licenseSha256, yamlParser version), none of which contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/source.json:1-11 records.

contracts/vendor/portkey-access/a27feb9/LICENSE:1-3 reads 'The MIT License / Copyright (c) OpenAI (https://openai.com)' although source.json:4 names https://github.com/Portkey-AI/openapi as the upstream repository.
A repository-wide grep for 'portkey-access-policies-research' returns no matches, so the rationale document is referenced by nothing.
limitations: Read-only tools and no network: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint de5a8957… or the recorded checks digest b556bd83…, re-execute tools/portkey-access.mjs, or re-run the unittest suites. I verified the recorded command list matches commands_for(15) and that the captured outputs are internally consistent, but the executions themselves are taken from docs/checks/phase-15.json.

Upstream identity of the vendored bytes cannot be established from inside the repository. I verified internal consistency and the parent-to-spec delta, but nothing available offline proves openapi.yaml and parent.yaml are the real Portkey-AI/openapi blobs at a27feb9 and 8f91369 — that is the substance of the source.json provenance finding.
